transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Do not check the magnetron or anything inside with the cover off. Microwaves retain a potentially lethal high-voltage charge even unplugged, and the high-voltage circuit is not a safe DIY test or repair. With the light, fan and turntable all working but no heat, the leading possibility is a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit; the magnetron is only one of several possible parts, alongside the diode, capacitor, transformer or—in some versions—an inverter board. First, refit the cover and make sure the screws are back in. Then safely check that it is set to full microwave power rather than defrost, grill or combination, using a cup of water for one minute. If it remains cold, it needs a microwave-qualified engineer or replacement rather than internal testing.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
It's unplugged now though, so surely it's safe? I've got a multimeter and I'm fairly handy. Is it really that risky?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Yes — it really is that risky, even unplugged. Please refit the cover and do not probe the magnetron or other internal parts. With the display, fan and turntable operating but no heat, the most likely issue is the high-voltage heating system; the exact failed item cannot be safely identified by DIY testing. A lower power/defrost or combination setting is the simpler alternative. Once the cover is back on, run a cup of water for one minute on full microwave power: is the water hot, or still cold? If still cold, arrange a microwave-qualified engineer or consider replacement.
